Classification history must remain immutable and auditable.  7. AUDIT RETENTION AND CONTENT-BEARING HISTORY  Content-free classification and decision audit metadata follows Q5's existing 365-day retention policy.  This must not be interpreted as permission to retain complete source documents, extracted content, conversation transcripts, or other content-bearing interaction history for 365 days. NON-NEGOTIABLE SECURITY AND GOVERNANCE BOUNDARIES  All Q1-Q5 decisions remain applicable.  In particular: - Classification does not imply document approval. - Priority does not imply escalation. - Queue suggestions do not imply ticket assignment. - Human approval does not bypass document validity or the 180-day re-review requirement. - Deleted, expired, superseded, rejected, and overdue content must retain their established retrieval restrictions. - Tenant isolation and role-based authorization remain mandatory. - Platform Admin tenant-content access remains prohibited in the first release. - No external integration or business action is authorized by classification requirements.  10. FINAL DECISION  The first release will deliver a common, centrally governed, human-reviewed classification and routing-suggestion foundation.  It will prioritize predictable classification, clear human accountability, historical traceability, tenant isolation, and controlled operational boundaries.  Advanced customization, automation, external integration, numeric thresholds, and content-bearing history retention remain explicitly deferred.  These clarifications record requirement decisions only. They do not constitute PRD approval, implementation authorization, permission to modify tickets, or authorization to start another process.

actual_fields.mapping_governance: TAXONOMY, PRIORITY AND ROUTING MAPPING CHANGE AUTHORITY POLICY  1. actual_fields.routing_suggestions: FIRST-RELEASE QUEUE AND ESCALATION SUGGESTION POLICY  1. SUPPORTED FIRST-RELEASE QUEUES  Adopt the following centrally defined synthetic/local queues:  1. PRODUCT_SUPPORT    Product functionality, features, specifications, and product-related issues.  3. ACCOUNT_ACCESS_SUPPORT    Login, authentication, user accounts, access permissions, and account-related issues.  4. BILLING_SUPPORT    Invoices, subscriptions, payment failures, refunds, and billing-related questions.  5. ORDER_SUPPORT    Order processing, order status, transactions, fulfilment, and delivery-related issues.  6. TECHNICAL_SUPPORT    Technical errors, troubleshooting, system failures, and integration-related technical questions.  7. POLICY_COMPLIANCE_SUPPORT    Business policies, terms and conditions, compliance, and regulatory-related questions.  8. actual_fields.override_history: HUMAN OVERRIDES AND RETAINED CLASSIFICATION EVIDENCE POLICY  1. IMMUTABLE ORIGINAL AI SUGGESTIONS  The system must preserve the original AI-generated classification and routing suggestions, even when a human reviewer accepts, rejects, or overrides them. HUMAN-CONFIRMED VALUES AND OVERRIDE HISTORY  For every human-reviewed classification, retain:  - Original AI-suggested values. - Human-confirmed category. - Human-confirmed priority. - Human-confirmed queue, where applicable. - Original and revised values for every override. - Reviewer identity and authorized role. - Review and decision timestamps. - Acceptance, rejection, or override decision. - Mandatory reason for material overrides. - Applicable taxonomy and mapping versions. FIRST-RELEASE DECISIONS  The first release adopts:  - Immutable original AI suggestions. - Immutable historical human decisions and overrides. - Complete taxonomy and mapping version traceability. - Reviewer identity, role, timestamps, and override reasons. - 365-day retention for content-free classification audit metadata. - Strict tenant-scoped, role-based audit access. - No persistent content-bearing interaction history until its separate retention policy is explicitly approved. Future priority-based automation, ticket integration, SLA mapping, configurable thresholds, and tenant-specific priority schemes are explicitly deferred and require separate approval.  These decisions define priority classification requirements only. They do not authorize PRD approval, implementation, or external business actions.,

mapping_governance.exact_rendered_segment: TAXONOMY, PRIORITY AND ROUTING MAPPING CHANGE AUTHORITY POLICY  1. FIRST-RELEASE CUSTOMIZATION BOUNDARY  - The first release uses centrally governed, common category, priority, and routing definitions. - Tenant-specific creation, modification, deletion, and customization of taxonomy values and mappings are deferred. - Tenants must not directly modify centrally governed category definitions, priority labels, or routing mappings. - This restriction applies consistently across all tenants. - Future tenant-specific customization requires separate explicit requirements, authorization, and governance approval.  2. CHANGE PROPOSAL AUTHORITY  The following roles may request or propose changes through a controlled governance process:  - Tenant Admin: May submit a change request based on tenant operational requirements. - Support Manager: May recommend changes based on operational experience and routing requirements. - Designated Product / Platform Governance Owner: May propose centrally governed taxonomy or mapping improvements.  A proposal is a request for consideration only. It does not authorize configuration changes or immediate application.  3. CHANGE APPROVAL AUTHORITY  - Changes to common taxonomy definitions, priority values, or routing mappings require approval from the designated Product / Platform Governance Owner. - The individual proposing a change must not approve their own proposal. - Approval must be independent, documented, and auditable. - Tenant-specific requests must undergo central governance review and must not be directly applied as tenant-specific overrides in the first release. - Administrative account-management privileges alone must not confer taxonomy governance or approval authority. - Platform Admin tenant-content access remains prohibited under the established first-release security boundary.  4. CHANGE APPLICATION AUTHORITY  - Only an authorized configuration-management service or explicitly designated configuration operator may apply approved changes. - Configuration changes must be applied through a controlled and auditable process. - An unapproved proposal must never modify active taxonomy, priority, or routing mappings. - Changes must be validated before becoming effective. - Application of a mapping change must not trigger automatic ticket creation, assignment, escalation, notifications, or other external business actions. - AI-generated mapping suggestions must remain non-authoritative until the required governance approval is completed.  5. VERSIONING AND EFFECTIVE DATES  Every approved mapping change must have:  - Unique mapping version identifier. - Previous and new mapping definitions. - Approval reference and approving authority. - Change reason and supporting rationale. - Effective-from timestamp. - Effective-to timestamp, where applicable. - Application timestamp. - Configuration operator or service identity. - Audit evidence of successful application.  All timestamps must be recorded in UTC.  Only one applicable active mapping version may govern a given classification operation at a particular effective time.  6. HISTORICAL CLASSIFICATION PRESERVATION  - Every classification record must preserve the mapping version used when the classification was created or approved. - Existing classification records must not be silently rewritten when a new mapping becomes effective. - Historical records must remain interpretable using their original mapping context. - New mapping versions apply prospectively from their approved effective date. - Any historical reclassification or migration must require a separately authorized and auditable process. - Historical classification changes must preserve the original values, previous mapping version, and reason for modification. - Mapping changes must not automatically change existing document approval, lifecycle, validity, retrieval eligibility, or priority confirmation status.  7. SEPARATION OF DUTIES  - Proposers must not approve their own changes. - Approvers must not bypass the designated governance process. - Configuration application must be restricted to authorized configuration identities. - Every proposal, approval, rejection, and application must be auditable. - Knowledge Reviewer permissions must not automatically include taxonomy administration privileges. - Tenant Admin and Platform Admin roles must not automatically confer central taxonomy approval authority.  8. AUDIT AND TRACEABILITY  Maintain an auditable history containing:  - Change request ID. - Requesting individual and role. - Proposed configuration changes. - Approval or rejection decision. - Approving individual and role. - Previous and new mapping versions. - Effective dates. - Application identity and timestamp. - Validation results. - Any application failure or rollback event.  Audit evidence must not expose unrelated tenant content or bypass existing tenant-isolation restrictions.  9. EXPLICITLY DEFERRED CAPABILITIES  The following capabilities are outside the first-release scope:  - Tenant-configurable categories and subcategories. - Tenant-specific priority labels and thresholds. - Tenant-specific routing overrides. - Self-service taxonomy administration. - Automated mapping approval. - Automatic historical reclassification. - Automatic ticket or external workflow integration.  These capabilities require separate requirements, governance decisions, and explicit authorization before implementation.  10. FINAL FIRST-RELEASE DECISION  Adopt a centrally governed, version-controlled taxonomy, priority, and routing mapping model.  Tenant Admins and Support Managers may request changes, but only the designated governance authority may approve them, and only authorized configuration services or operators may apply them.  Historical classification context must remain immutable and traceable.  Tenant-specific customization remains deferred for the first release.  These decisions clarify change authority and configuration governance only. They do not authorize PRD approval, implementation, external integrations, or any bypass of established Q1-Q5 security and lifecycle restrictions.,

routing_suggestions.exact_rendered_segment: FIRST-RELEASE QUEUE AND ESCALATION SUGGESTION POLICY  1. SUPPORTED FIRST-RELEASE QUEUES  Adopt the following centrally defined synthetic/local queues:  1. GENERAL_SUPPORT    General questions, information requests, and support matters that do not clearly belong to another specialized queue.  2. PRODUCT_SUPPORT    Product functionality, features, specifications, and product-related issues.  3. ACCOUNT_ACCESS_SUPPORT    Login, authentication, user accounts, access permissions, and account-related issues.  4. BILLING_SUPPORT    Invoices, subscriptions, payment failures, refunds, and billing-related questions.  5. ORDER_SUPPORT    Order processing, order status, transactions, fulfilment, and delivery-related issues.  6. TECHNICAL_SUPPORT    Technical errors, troubleshooting, system failures, and integration-related technical questions.  7. POLICY_COMPLIANCE_SUPPORT    Business policies, terms and conditions, compliance, and regulatory-related questions.  8. UNASSIGNED_REVIEW    Ambiguous, unsupported, conflicting, or insufficiently documented requests requiring human assessment.  These queues are synthetic/local classifications only. No external ticketing system, CRM, support platform, or third-party integration is included in the first release.  2. QUEUE SUGGESTION CRITERIA  AI may suggest a queue using:  - Approved document category and classification metadata. - User-reported issue and its actual context. - Relevant supporting evidence from eligible knowledge. - Nature of the reported problem. - Business function or product capability affected. - Available supporting information and classification confidence.  Queue suggestions must be evidence-based.  The AI must not invent an operational team, queue, department, or external destination.  Where multiple queues are plausible, evidence is insufficient, or the issue falls outside supported categories, the system must suggest UNASSIGNED_REVIEW.  3. ESCALATION SUGGESTION CRITERIA  AI may recommend human escalation review when available evidence indicates:  - Potential widespread service disruption. - Material impact on a critical business function. - A potentially serious security or availability issue. - Repeated failures affecting important operations. - Significant unresolved operational impact.  Every escalation suggestion must include: - Reason for the suggestion. - Supporting evidence. - Affected capability or business function, where known. - Relevant uncertainty or missing information. - Recommended human review.  AI must not invent incident severity, affected-user counts, contractual obligations, or SLA breaches.  An escalation suggestion is advisory only and does not constitute an approved incident classification or escalation decision.  4. HUMAN REVIEW AND DECISION AUTHORITY  Support Agent: - Reviews AI-generated queue suggestions. - May accept or reject a suggestion within their authorized responsibilities. - May request additional information. - May recommend a different queue. - Must not bypass existing authorization or governance controls.  Support Manager: - Reviews disputed, conflicting, or significant routing recommendations. - May accept, reject, or override a suggested queue. - Makes the authorized human decision regarding escalation recommendations. - Must provide a reason for material overrides.  A person must not approve their own restricted or unauthorized actions.  AI suggestions must remain non-authoritative until the applicable human decision is recorded.  5. UNCERTAIN AND CONFLICTING CASES  - Insufficient evidence must result in UNASSIGNED_REVIEW. - Conflicting category and routing evidence must be flagged for human review. - Unsupported queue destinations must never be invented. - Low-confidence suggestions must clearly communicate uncertainty. - The system must preserve the original AI suggestion and subsequent human decision. - AI must not repeatedly generate alternative suggestions to bypass a human rejection. - Unresolved cases must remain pending human review rather than being automatically escalated.  6. AUDIT AND TRACEABILITY  Record the following information:  - Request or classification reference. - AI-suggested queue. - Supporting rationale and evidence. - AI suggestion timestamp. - Suggested escalation status and reason, where applicable. - Reviewing individual's identity and role. - Accepted, rejected, or overridden decision. - Final human-confirmed queue. - Human decision timestamp. - Reason for any override or rejection.  Maintain the original AI suggestion separately from the final human decision.  7. STRICT FIRST-RELEASE ACTION RESTRICTIONS  The first release is limited to synthetic/local-only suggestions.  AI must not: - Create support tickets. - Assign tickets to external teams. - Change existing ticket status or priority. - Automatically escalate issues. - Trigger external workflows. - Send emails, notifications, or messages. - Write back to CRM, ITSM, or other external systems. - Invoke integration tools to modify business records.  All queue and escalation suggestions must remain within the local application boundary established by Q1.  8. PRIORITY AND ESCALATION SEPARATION  Priority classification, queue routing, and escalation recommendation are separate decisions.  - P1/P2 priority suggestions do not automatically trigger escalation. - A high-priority classification does not automatically create an incident. - Queue assignment suggestions do not establish an SLA. - An escalation recommendation requires separate human review and authorization. - Existing priority confirmation and taxonomy governance rules remain applicable.  9. EXPLICIT FIRST-RELEASE DECISIONS  The first release adopts: - Eight centrally defined synthetic/local queues. - Evidence-based AI routing suggestions. - UNASSIGNED_REVIEW as the fallback. - Advisory-only escalation recommendations. - Support Agent review and Support Manager oversight. - Auditable human acceptance, rejection, and override decisions. - No automatic ticket creation, assignment, escalation, external messaging, or integration writebacks.  External queue integration, automated ticket routing, SLA-based escalation, notification workflows, and tenant-configurable queues are explicitly deferred and require separate requirements and authorization.  These decisions define routing and escalation suggestion requirements only. They do not authorize PRD approval, implementation, external integrations, or any bypass of Q1-Q5 governance and security restrictions.,

override_history.exact_rendered_segment: HUMAN OVERRIDES AND RETAINED CLASSIFICATION EVIDENCE POLICY  1. IMMUTABLE ORIGINAL AI SUGGESTIONS  The system must preserve the original AI-generated classification and routing suggestions, even when a human reviewer accepts, rejects, or overrides them.  The following information must be retained:  - Original AI-suggested category. - Original AI-suggested priority. - Original AI-suggested queue. - Original escalation recommendation, where applicable. - AI-generated rationale and content-free supporting evidence references. - AI suggestion timestamp. - Applicable taxonomy and mapping version identifiers.  Original AI suggestions must never be silently overwritten by subsequent human decisions or AI reclassification.  2. HUMAN-CONFIRMED VALUES AND OVERRIDE HISTORY  For every human-reviewed classification, retain:  - Original AI-suggested values. - Human-confirmed category. - Human-confirmed priority. - Human-confirmed queue, where applicable. - Original and revised values for every override. - Reviewer identity and authorized role. - Review and decision timestamps. - Acceptance, rejection, or override decision. - Mandatory reason for material overrides. - Applicable taxonomy and mapping versions.  Each subsequent change must create a new auditable decision record.  Previous classification decisions must remain available as historical evidence and must not be silently modified or deleted.  3. TAXONOMY AND MAPPING VERSION PRESERVATION  Every classification decision must retain the exact taxonomy and mapping version applicable at the time of that decision.  - Historical records must remain associated with their original mapping version. - Future mapping changes must not rewrite historical classifications. - Any authorized historical reclassification must preserve the original decision, new decision, reason, reviewer, and timestamps. - Historical classification evidence must remain interpretable without depending on the currently active taxonomy.  4. CONTENT-FREE AUDIT RETENTION — 365 DAYS  Adopt the existing Q5 policy of 365-day retention for content-free classification and decision audit metadata.  This includes:  - Opaque document and classification references. - Original AI-suggested values. - Human-confirmed values. - Previous and revised values. - Taxonomy and mapping version identifiers. - Reviewer identity and role. - Decision timestamps. - Content-free override reasons. - Decision and approval status.  The audit record must not contain complete source documents, extracted document text, full conversation transcripts, or unnecessary sensitive content.  The 365-day retention period applies to content-free audit metadata only and does not automatically authorize retention of content-bearing interaction history.  5. ACCESS CONTROL AND TENANT ISOLATION  - Classification history must be accessible only to explicitly authorized users within the relevant tenant and designated governance/audit roles. - Tenant Admins and authorized Support Managers may access records only within their assigned responsibilities. - Knowledge Reviewers may access classification evidence required for their authorized review duties. - Access must follow least-privilege principles. - Platform Admins must not gain tenant-content access through audit or classification permissions. - All access to protected classification history must be tenant-scoped and auditable. - One tenant must never be able to inspect another tenant's classification evidence.  6. CONTENT-BEARING INTERACTION HISTORY — EXPLICIT DEFERRAL  Full conversation transcripts, source-document excerpts, original prompts, extracted content, and other content-bearing interaction history require a separate retention and access policy.  This policy is explicitly deferred.  Before enabling persistent storage of such information, the following must be decided:  - Exact content permitted to be retained. - Purpose and justification for retention. - Authorized access roles. - Tenant isolation requirements. - Retention duration and deletion triggers. - Handling of deletion requests and Legal Holds. - Sensitive information and secret exclusion rules. - Verification of physical deletion.  Until these decisions are explicitly approved, the system must not introduce persistent content-bearing classification interaction history as an implied extension of the 365-day audit policy.  7. SEPARATION FROM DOCUMENT LIFECYCLE AND DELETION  Classification audit retention must not override Q2/Q3/Q4/Q5 controls.  - Deleted or deletion-approved document content must not be restored through classification history. - Classification audit metadata must not contain retained copies of deleted business content. - Content-free audit evidence may remain under the approved 365-day policy. - Legal Hold and deletion rules must continue to apply independently. - Retaining classification metadata must never imply document retrieval eligibility or permission to access the original content.  8. FIRST-RELEASE DECISIONS  The first release adopts:  - Immutable original AI suggestions. - Immutable historical human decisions and overrides. - Complete taxonomy and mapping version traceability. - Reviewer identity, role, timestamps, and override reasons. - 365-day retention for content-free classification audit metadata. - Strict tenant-scoped, role-based audit access. - No persistent content-bearing interaction history until its separate retention policy is explicitly approved.  The retention duration and detailed governance for content-bearing interaction history remain deferred and constitute a decision gate before the affected capability proceeds.  These decisions define classification evidence and audit requirements only. They do not authorize PRD approval, implementation, additional content retention, or any bypass of Q1-Q5 security and lifecycle controls.,

rationale_deferrals.exact_rendered_segment: Q6 — RATIONALE, FIRST-RELEASE BOUNDARY AND EXPLICIT DEFERRALS  1. FIRST-RELEASE DESIGN RATIONALE  The first release adopts a common, centrally governed taxonomy and classification model across all tenants.  The objective is to establish a consistent, auditable, predictable, and secure classification foundation before introducing tenant-specific complexity or automated operational workflows.  The selected approach separates: - AI-generated classification suggestions. - Human-confirmed classification decisions. - Priority assessment. - Queue routing suggestions. - Escalation recommendations. - Actual operational actions.  This separation prevents AI recommendations from silently becoming authoritative business decisions.  2. CONFIRMED FIRST-RELEASE TAXONOMY  The first release adopts eight centrally defined categories:  - PRODUCT_AND_FEATURES - ACCOUNT_AND_ACCESS - BILLING_AND_PAYMENTS - ORDERS_AND_TRANSACTIONS - TECHNICAL_SUPPORT - HOW_TO_AND_USER_GUIDES - POLICIES_AND_COMPLIANCE - OTHER_UNCLASSIFIED  OTHER_UNCLASSIFIED is the fallback when evidence is insufficient, ambiguous, conflicting, or unsupported.  AI must not invent new categories or silently force an unsupported classification into an unrelated category.  3. CONFIRMED PRIORITY POLICY  The first release adopts:  - P1 — CRITICAL - P2 — HIGH - P3 — NORMAL - P4 — LOW - UNASSESSED — Default when evidence is insufficient.  Priority suggestions must be evidence-based and accompanied by a rationale.  AI-generated priority remains advisory. Only an authorized human decision establishes the authoritative priority.  No numeric confidence thresholds, automated priority-based escalation rules, or SLA commitments are introduced without separate approval.  4. CONFIRMED QUEUE AND ESCALATION POLICY  The first release adopts eight synthetic/local queues:  - GENERAL_SUPPORT - PRODUCT_SUPPORT - ACCOUNT_ACCESS_SUPPORT - BILLING_SUPPORT - ORDER_SUPPORT - TECHNICAL_SUPPORT - POLICY_COMPLIANCE_SUPPORT - UNASSIGNED_REVIEW  AI may suggest queues and recommend human escalation review based on available evidence.  Support Agents may review and accept or reject suggestions within their authorized responsibilities. Support Managers provide oversight for disputed or significant routing and escalation decisions.  No automatic ticket creation, assignment, escalation, external writeback, outgoing communication, or integration-tool action is permitted.  5. CENTRAL GOVERNANCE AND VERSION CONTROL  Taxonomy, priority, and routing mappings remain centrally governed.  - Tenant-specific customization is outside the first-release scope. - Change proposals, approvals, and application must remain separate responsibilities. - The proposer must not approve their own change. - Approved mappings must be version-controlled and have explicit effective dates. - Historical classifications must retain the original mapping version. - Existing records must not be silently rewritten when mappings change. - Any historical reclassification requires a separately authorized and auditable process.  6. HUMAN REVIEW AND CLASSIFICATION EVIDENCE  AI suggestions are recommendations, not authoritative decisions.  The system must preserve: - Original AI suggestions. - Original taxonomy and mapping versions. - Human-confirmed category, priority, and queue. - Reviewer identity and authorized role. - Decision timestamps. - Original and revised values. - Reasons for overrides, rejections, and material changes.  Classification history must remain immutable and auditable.  7. AUDIT RETENTION AND CONTENT-BEARING HISTORY  Content-free classification and decision audit metadata follows Q5's existing 365-day retention policy.  This must not be interpreted as permission to retain complete source documents, extracted content, conversation transcripts, or other content-bearing interaction history for 365 days.  Persistent content-bearing interaction history remains explicitly deferred.  Its retention duration, access authority, deletion triggers, legal-hold handling, sensitive-content exclusions, and physical deletion verification must be separately decided before the affected capability proceeds.  8. EXPLICITLY DEFERRED TAXONOMY AND CLASSIFICATION CAPABILITIES  The following are outside the first-release scope:  - Tenant-specific categories and subcategories. - Hierarchical and customizable taxonomy structures. - Tenant-specific priority labels and thresholds. - Numeric AI confidence thresholds. - Automatic classification approval. - Automatic historical reclassification. - Advanced classification analytics. - Automated queue assignment. - Automatic escalation and SLA-based routing. - External ticketing and CRM integration. - Automated notifications and business workflows. - Persistent content-bearing interaction history. - Detailed retention schedules for content-bearing classification evidence.  These are deferred capabilities, not implicitly approved future implementations. Each requires explicit requirements, governance review, and authorization.  9. NON-NEGOTIABLE SECURITY AND GOVERNANCE BOUNDARIES  All Q1-Q5 decisions remain applicable.  In particular: - Classification does not imply document approval. - Priority does not imply escalation. - Queue suggestions do not imply ticket assignment. - Human approval does not bypass document validity or the 180-day re-review requirement. - Deleted, expired, superseded, rejected, and overdue content must retain their established retrieval restrictions. - Tenant isolation and role-based authorization remain mandatory. - Platform Admin tenant-content access remains prohibited in the first release. - No external integration or business action is authorized by classification requirements.  10. FINAL DECISION  The first release will deliver a common, centrally governed, human-reviewed classification and routing-suggestion foundation.  It will prioritize predictable classification, clear human accountability, historical traceability, tenant isolation, and controlled operational boundaries.  Advanced customization, automation, external integration, numeric thresholds, and content-bearing history retention remain explicitly deferred.  These clarifications record requirement decisions only. They do not constitute PRD approval, implementation authorization, permission to modify tickets, or authorization to start another process.
